questions.question: What does Product structured data actually enable beyond a visual rich snippet in search results?
questions.answer_summary: Google's own docs state it enables Google Shopping tab placement, Merchant Center integration, shopping knowledge panels with seller info, popular-product carousels, and enriched Google Images/Lens results — not just a prettier blue link.

questions.question: What's the difference between 'product snippets' and 'merchant listings' markup?
questions.answer_summary: Product snippets are for editorial/review pages without direct purchase; merchant listings are for pages where customers can actually buy, and support sizing, shipping, and return-policy detail.

questions.question: If I already submit a Merchant Center feed, do I still need on-page structured data?
questions.answer_summary: Google explicitly recommends both: 'Providing both structured data on web pages and a Merchant Center feed maximizes your eligibility to experiences and helps Google correctly understand and verify your data.'

questions.question: What specific product attributes should be marked up, and why do they matter to Google Shopping?
questions.answer_summary: Properties align to Merchant Center feed attributes (product_type, google_product_category, unit pricing) plus identifiers like GTIN/SKU/MPN, so markup and feed data stay consistent for shopping surfaces.

questions.question: Does schema markup help pages surface in AI Overviews / generative search, not just classic organic results?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — practitioner discussion frames structured data (including FAQPage/HowTo/Product schema) as one of the direct levers for AI Overview inclusion, alongside entity clarity and E-E-A-T signals.

questions.question: What is GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) and how does schema fit into it?
questions.answer_summary: A growing tool category (geo-lint, BetterAEO, Cloro.dev) explicitly scores/validates structured data as part of 'AI-citation readiness' for tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews.

questions.question: Is Product schema used by anything other than Google?
questions.answer_summary: Schema.org documents adoption across 10M+ domains and describes consumers beyond search engines, including comparison tools and supply-chain/product-catalog systems that parse the same markup.

questions.question: Can third-party tools/scrapers rely on product schema to extract catalog data without an API?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — a developer building a car-marketplace data visualization noted that sites using schema.org/Product 'simplify things' for scraping, even without official APIs.

questions.question: Does return-policy/shipping data in merchant listing markup actually change buyer behavior?
questions.answer_summary: Google's guidance frames this data as functional, not decorative — it surfaces pricing, availability, shipping cost, and return policy directly in the shopping surfaces where buyers decide whether to click through.

questions.question: What product schema properties support 'complex' catalogs (variants, bundles, digital products)?
questions.answer_summary: Schema.org's Product type supports variant/group relationships, energy-consumption data, and accessory/consumable/similar-product relationships for more complex catalog structures, not just a flat price+name+image model.
